column1: # The code checks of lesson P/03: rows of the kinds of the closed dictionary
# Platform/common/acceptance/forms/code-rules.tsv, which defines the columns, the outcome and the
# checks; no expected answer. name: the name that the profile field code (of the profile of 03-worker) maps to a symbol of the candidate; the names
# are not code paths. stage: the stage of forms/stages.tsv from which the row holds, under the gate code:* of that stage and of every later stage that
# holds code:*. norm: the norms of the subject. Cores: capture_core (the capture of a slot), lease_core (epoch issue and lease confirmation),
# heartbeat_core (the heartbeat object and the memory budget decision), reconcile_core (the plan of one loop turn), open_core (open or Sealed with
# its cause over bytes already read), holder_core (the holder's look), contender_core (the contender mark), token_core (the domain token at the
# worker and at the recipient); their machines in the form Step(State, Event) -> (State, []Effect) are capture_step, contender_step and
# token_cache_step. Wall-clock reads, the tick and the local calendar day are inputs that the ordinary core supplies (forms/README.md), so time in
# forbid does not bar them. The CEL cells of forms/slot-capture.tsv and of daemon-flags.tsv run in the adapter and the kit, not in the core: no cel
# row and no table_driven row of slot-capture.tsv. The pinned JSON Schema validator of the data families is a requires_module row of stage
# sdk_model. The refusals of chapters 3.2, 3.4–3.7 are one form: one table_driven row, exhaustive over its column surface (its column kind is -).
